title: Victoria to pay cost of returning body of man shot by police to Prince Rupert
article: The provincial government has agreed to cover the cost of returning the body of Gerald Chenery back home to Prince Rupert.
The 29-year-old man, who was shot to death by Vancouver police on Boxing Day, was in the morgue of a Vancouver hospital for almost two weeks before being transferred to a Squamish funeral home.
"My brother and his wife heard \[the Ministry of Human Resources\] gave the go-ahead to have him sent home for burial," said Teresa Chenery, the dead man's sister. "It was a very big surprise."

Chenery, who is on income assistance and supports six children, had been told by the ministry that it would not cover bereavement costs. Left with no other option, she appealed to the public for help to bring her brother's body home.
"It was hard after I found out \[Gerald\] wouldn't be sent \[home\]," she said.
"I was asking everybody, nothing was happening for the longest time. They had said they were going to cremate him."

Chenery spoke with North Coast Victim Services in Prince Rupert, which passed on information to a senior ministry official in the Lower Mainland. Media attention brought Chenery's plight to the attention of Minister of Human Resources Susan Brice, whose office helped facilitate the decision.

The family will now set about making funeral, memorial and feast arrangements. But with a guarantee the body will be returned to Prince Rupert, some members of Chenery's family are turning their attention to the police action that took his life.
The family believes Chenery may have been shot as many as 15 times. Police will not reveal how many times Chenery was shot because it is part of an investigation.

Vancouver police say two officers stopped Gerald Chenery in an alley in the 200 block of East Hastings. When they checked his name, they found he was wanted on a Canada-wide warrant for failing to report to a halfway house after being released from jail.
The officers tried to arrest him, police say, but Chenery pulled a knife and lunged at one of the officers before he was shot.

"I want to know how many times he was shot and if it was justifiable," said Leonard Lincoln, Gerald's half-brother. Lincoln said he could understand police shooting a man with a knife "two or three" times, but the number of rounds fired concerns him.
